subject: Michael Jackson
clues: He started performing with his brothers as a child.
He was famous for a dance move that made it look like he was walking backwards.
He had a pet chimpanzee named Bubbles.
His album Thriller is the best-selling album of all time.
He was known as the King of Pop.
This American singer recorded Billie Jean, Beat It, and Thriller.

subject: The Titanic
clues: It happened on a ship's very first journey.
It sank after hitting a large block of ice in the ocean.
A 1997 Leonardo DiCaprio film told a love story set during this disaster.
More than 1,500 people died because there were not enough lifeboats.
It happened in the North Atlantic Ocean in April 1912.
This famous ship sank on its maiden voyage and became one of history's most famous disasters.

subject: The Eiffel Tower
clues: It was built for a world's fair in 1889.
It is made entirely of iron and painted a brownish color.
It has a restaurant and observation deck near the top.
Millions of tourists visit it every year to take the same photo.
It lights up at night and is in the center of one of Europe's most famous cities.
This iconic iron tower is the most recognizable symbol of Paris, France.

subject: Harry Potter
clues: Its main character finds out on his 11th birthday that he is a wizard.
The story takes place mostly at a school called Hogwarts.
A lightning bolt scar on the hero's forehead is a key detail.
It was written by a British author who came up with the idea on a delayed train.
Daniel Radcliffe played the lead character in eight films.
This is J.K. Rowling's series about a young wizard who must defeat the dark lord Voldemort.

subject: The Moon Landing
clues: It happened in the summer of 1969.
Two men walked on a surface while a third waited in orbit above them.
The words 'one small step for man' were spoken live on television.
It was part of a space race between the United States and the Soviet Union.
Hundreds of millions of people watched it live on television.
NASA's Apollo 11 mission landed the first humans on the Moon on July 20, 1969.

subject: Leonardo da Vinci
clues: He filled notebooks with drawings of flying machines, anatomy, and inventions centuries before they existed.
He painted on a wall inside a Milan dining hall — and the paint started peeling almost immediately.
He was left-handed and wrote his notes in mirror script.
He painted the most famous portrait in the world — a woman with no eyebrows and a mysterious smile.
He was born in Italy in 1452 and is considered the ultimate Renaissance man.
This Italian genius painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper.

subject: The Olympics
clues: It began in ancient Greece over 2,700 years ago.
Athletes from almost every country in the world compete in it.
Its symbol is five interlocking rings in different colors.
It alternates every two years between a summer and winter version.
The winner of each event receives a gold medal.
This international sporting competition is held every four years and is the world's biggest athletic event.

subject: Cleopatra
clues: She ruled one of the ancient world's most powerful kingdoms.
She was actually Greek by ancestry, not from the country she ruled.
She formed powerful romantic alliances with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony.
She is said to have died from a snake bite.
She was the last pharaoh before her kingdom was taken over by Rome.
This queen of ancient Egypt is one of the most famous women in history.

subject: The Great Wall of China
clues: It was built over many centuries by emperors to protect their kingdom.
Millions of workers — including soldiers and prisoners — built it by hand.
It runs through mountains, deserts, and grasslands across northern China.
It is one of the most visited tourist attractions on Earth.
Despite popular myth, it cannot actually be seen from space with the naked eye.
This ancient stone wall stretching thousands of miles is one of the greatest construction projects in human history.

subject: Usain Bolt
clues: He grew up in a small town in Jamaica and was a natural athlete from childhood.
He once celebrated before crossing the finish line — and still set a world record.
He won gold medals at three consecutive Olympic Games.
His world record of 9.58 seconds in the 100 meters has never been beaten.
He is so much faster than everyone else that his races are often decided before the finish line.
This Jamaican sprinter is the fastest human being ever recorded.

subject: World War II
clues: It involved countries from almost every continent on Earth.
It began in Europe in 1939 and ended in 1945.
The Holocaust — the murder of six million Jewish people — happened during this conflict.
It ended in the Pacific after the United States dropped two atomic bombs on Japan.
It was the deadliest conflict in human history, killing an estimated 70 to 85 million people.
This global war fought between 1939 and 1945 remains the largest and most destructive in human history.

subject: The iPhone
clues: Before it existed, phones had physical keyboards and tiny screens.
It was announced by a CEO in jeans and a black turtleneck on a stage in San Francisco.
It combined a phone, a music player, and an internet browser into one device.
Its app store created an entirely new economy of software developers.
It completely changed how humans interact with technology in less than a decade.
Apple's Steve Jobs unveiled this revolutionary smartphone in 2007.

subject: Nelson Mandela
clues: He spent 27 years in prison for opposing a racist government system.
He was held on a small island where he broke rocks in a quarry.
When he was released in 1990, millions of people watched it live on television.
He shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.
He became his country's first democratically elected president.
This South African leader ended apartheid and became a global symbol of forgiveness and freedom.

subject: Minecraft
clues: It was created by a single Swedish developer and sold from a basic website.
Players collect materials and use them to build almost anything they can imagine.
It has no fixed goal — you can survive, create, or explore endlessly.
It is the best-selling video game of all time with over 300 million copies sold.
Its blocky visual style is now one of the most recognized aesthetics in the world.
This sandbox video game created by Markus Persson lets players build anything out of blocks.

subject: The Amazon Rainforest
clues: It produces so much oxygen it is sometimes called the lungs of the Earth.
It is home to more species of plant and animal than anywhere else on the planet.
It covers large parts of Brazil and several neighboring South American countries.
Deforestation is destroying large sections of it every year.
The world's largest river runs through it.
This vast tropical forest in South America is the largest rainforest on Earth.

subject: Lionel Messi
clues: He grew up in Argentina and moved to Spain as a child to join a famous football club.
He won the Ballon d'Or — the award for the world's best player — eight times.
He spent most of his career at FC Barcelona.
He finally won the World Cup with Argentina in 2022 after three previous attempts.
Many people consider him the greatest footballer who ever lived.
This Argentine forward is widely regarded as the best football player in history.

subject: The Pyramids of Giza
clues: They were built as tombs for rulers of an ancient civilization.
The largest one was the tallest man-made structure in the world for nearly 4,000 years.
They were built without modern machinery — exactly how is still debated.
A large stone sculpture with a human head and lion's body sits nearby.
They are located on the edge of a major African city beside a famous river.
These ancient stone monuments near Cairo, Egypt are one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

subject: Breaking Bad
clues: Its main character starts out as a mild-mannered high school teacher.
He begins making drugs after being diagnosed with terminal cancer.
It is set in the desert landscape of New Mexico.
The main character uses the criminal alias Heisenberg.
Bryan Cranston won four Emmy Awards for playing Walter White.
This AMC television series follows a chemistry teacher who builds a methamphetamine empire.

subject: Marie Curie
clues: She grew up in Poland at a time when women were not allowed to attend university there.
She moved to Paris to study and worked in conditions so cold her water bottle froze at her desk.
She discovered two new elements and named one of them after her home country.
She was the first person ever to win Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields.
Her notebooks are still so radioactive they are kept in lead-lined boxes.
This Polish-French scientist was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.

subject: Instagram
clues: It was launched in 2010 and reached one million users in its first two months.
It was originally only available on iPhone.
Facebook bought it for one billion dollars in 2012 — considered a bargain within years.
It changed how people share food, travel, and personal moments with strangers.
Its square photo format and filters defined a visual aesthetic for an entire decade.
This photo and video sharing app is one of the most used social media platforms in the world.

subject: Fairuz
clues: She was discovered as a teenager singing in a radio choir in Beirut.
Her voice was played on the radio every morning — entire cities would stop to listen.
She refused to perform during the Lebanese Civil War.
She is called the ambassador of Lebanon to the stars.
Her songs are still heard in every Arab home, café, and taxi decades after they were recorded.
This Lebanese singer is the most beloved Arab vocalist of the 20th century.

subject: Chernobyl
clues: It happened because of a safety test that went catastrophically wrong.
An entire city of 50,000 people was abandoned overnight and never returned to.
The explosion sent radioactive material across large parts of Europe.
A 2019 HBO series dramatized the disaster and became one of the highest rated TV shows ever made.
It happened in 1986 in what is now Ukraine, during the era of the Soviet Union.
This nuclear power plant explosion is the worst nuclear disaster in human history.

subject: The Colosseum
clues: It was built over 2,000 years ago and could hold up to 80,000 spectators.
Gladiators fought each other and wild animals inside it.
It is still standing today despite earthquakes and centuries of use as a stone quarry.
It has 80 entrance arches and could be filled or emptied of crowds in minutes.
It is the most visited ancient monument in the world.
This massive ancient Roman arena in the center of Rome hosted gladiatorial combat for centuries.

subject: Frida Kahlo
clues: She was badly injured in a bus accident as a teenager and began painting while recovering in bed.
She is famous for her self-portraits and her distinctive unibrow.
She was Mexican and her paintings often referenced indigenous culture and personal pain.
She married the famous muralist Diego Rivera — twice.
Her face is now one of the most reproduced images in the history of art.
This Mexican painter is one of the most famous female artists of the 20th century.

subject: The Berlin Wall
clues: It was built overnight in 1961, separating families who woke up on different sides.
Guards were ordered to shoot anyone trying to cross it illegally.
Ronald Reagan stood near it in 1987 and demanded it be torn down.
When it fell in November 1989, crowds gathered and began breaking it apart with hammers.
Its fall marked the end of the Cold War and the reunification of a divided country.
This concrete barrier divided East and West Germany — and the city of Berlin — for 28 years.

subject: SpongeBob SquarePants
clues: It is set in an underwater city called Bikini Bottom.
The main character works as a fry cook at a fast food restaurant called the Krusty Krab.
His best friend is a pink starfish named Patrick.
It has been running since 1999 and has spawned movies, musicals, and theme park rides.
Its creator was a marine biology teacher who wanted to make a cartoon about ocean life.
This Nickelodeon animated series follows a cheerful sea sponge and is one of the most watched cartoons ever made.

subject: The Amazon River
clues: It flows through the largest tropical rainforest on Earth.
It releases more fresh water into the ocean than any other river in the world.
Pink dolphins are one of the unique animals found in its waters.
It runs through Brazil and several other South American countries.
Its mouth is so wide that early explorers didn't realize it was a river.
This South American river is the largest river in the world by volume of water.

subject: The Hunger Games
clues: It is set in a future version of North America divided into districts controlled by a wealthy Capitol.
Every year, two young people from each district are chosen to fight to the death on live television.
The main character volunteers to take her younger sister's place.
Jennifer Lawrence played the lead character in four films.
The protagonist's weapon of choice is a bow and arrow.
This Suzanne Collins novel series follows Katniss Everdeen in a dystopian society that forces children to fight.

subject: Machu Picchu
clues: It sits so high in the mountains that clouds pass through it.
It was built by the Inca civilization without the use of wheels or iron tools.
It was unknown to the outside world until an American explorer found it in 1911.
Its stones fit so perfectly together that no mortar was needed.
It is one of the most visited ancient sites in South America.
This Incan citadel high in the Peruvian Andes is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

subject: Albert Einstein
clues: He developed some of his most important ideas while working as a clerk reviewing patent applications.
Born in Germany, he spent much of his adult life in Switzerland before settling in the United States.
As a child he was late to speak, and teachers thought he would never amount to much.
He won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921 — but not for his most famous work.
His equation E=mc² showed that mass and energy are two forms of the same thing.
This German-born physicist developed the theory of relativity and became the most famous scientist of the 20th century.
